indication.text: BRIVIACT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

citations.quote: BRIVIACT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

target_moa.text: Brivaracetam has a high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain, which is considered the primary mechanism for its anticonvulsant activity.

citations.quote: Brivaracetam displays a high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain. Binding to SV2A is considered to be the primary mechanism for BRV anticonvulsant activity.
The chemical name of brivaracetam (BRV) is (2S)-2-[(4R)-2-oxo-4-propyltetrahydro-1H-pyrrol-1-yl] butanamide which is a 2-pyrrolidone derivative.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and ≥2% more than placebo) at doses ≥50 mg/day: somnolence and sedation (16% vs 8% placebo), dizziness (12% vs 7%), fatigue (9% vs 4%), and nausea/vomiting symptoms (5% vs 3%). Warnings include suicidal behavior and ideation, and neurological adverse reactions.

summary.text: Standard NDA reviewed as a traditional (non-accelerated) approval; not referred to an advisory committee. Approval was based on three adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, with deferred pediatric studies required as postmarketing requirements under PREA.

Priority or Standard	Standard

The applicant has provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for the use of brivaracetam as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years and older with epilepsy. This conclusion is supported by evidence from three adequate and well-controlled studies (studies 1252, 1253, and 1358) that evaluated the use of brivaracetam at various doses.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 505B(a) of the FDCA are required postmarketing studies.
